title: Salary Cap exists for every Salary Cap Year
summary: Each Salary Cap Year of the agreement has a Salary Cap that limits team spending.
detail_paraphrase: For every Salary Cap Year covered by the CBA there is a Salary Cap. The base Salary Cap equals 44.74% of Projected BRI for that year, minus Projected Benefits for that year, with the result divided by the number of teams scheduled to play in the NBA that year (excluding Expansion Teams during their first two Salary Cap Years).
conditions: A Salary Cap Year covered by the term of the agreement
exceptions: Expansion Teams in their first two Salary Cap Years are excluded from the team count divisor
Alternative expansion-driven calculation under CAP-002 may control
thresholds: 44.74% of Projected BRI, less Projected Benefits, divided by number of non-first-two-year-expansion teams

title: Expansion-adjusted Salary Cap override
summary: In a year an Expansion Team plays its second season, an alternative cap calculation applies if it yields a higher cap.
detail_paraphrase: When one or more Expansion Teams is scheduled to play its second season in a given year, an alternative cap is computed: take Projected BRI plus Projected Local Expansion Team BRI for that year, multiply by the same 44.74% percentage, subtract Projected Benefits (including for the Expansion Team(s)), then divide by the number of teams scheduled to play that year (including the Expansion Team(s)). If this alternative figure exceeds the standard cap from CAP-001, the Salary Cap equals this alternative figure instead.
conditions: One or more Expansion Teams scheduled to play its second season in the Salary Cap Year
The alternative figure exceeds the standard Salary Cap
applies_to: all teams in a year with a second-season Expansion Team
thresholds: (Projected BRI + Projected Local Expansion Team BRI) x 44.74% less Projected Benefits, divided by total teams including expansion teams

title: Interim Audit Report true-up adjustment
summary: Differences between an Interim Audit Report and the final Audit Report are credited or debited to a later Salary Cap.
detail_paraphrase: If a Salary Cap was set using an Interim Audit Report for the prior year, and the final Audit Report shows different BRI and Total Salaries and Benefits that would have produced a different cap, the difference is debited or credited (with interest at the one-year Treasury Bill rate published in The Wall Street Journal on the Interim Audit Report issuance date) to the subsequent Salary Cap Year. For the 2029-30 year (or 2028-29 if either party exercises the Article XXXIX termination option), the adjustment instead applies to the then-current year.
conditions: Salary Cap for a year was based on an Interim Audit Report under CAP-014
Final Audit Report figures differ such that the cap would have differed
exceptions: For 2029-30 (or 2028-29 if early termination), the adjustment hits the then-current year instead of the subsequent year
thresholds: Difference carried with interest at the 1-year Treasury Bill rate (WSJ, Interim Audit Report issuance date)

title: Minimum Team Salary set at 90% of cap
summary: The Minimum Team Salary each year equals 90% of the Salary Cap.
detail_paraphrase: For each Salary Cap Year, the Minimum Team Salary is fixed at ninety percent of that year's Salary Cap.
exceptions: Expansion Teams use 90% of their reduced First/Second Year Expansion Team Salary Cap (see CAP-027)
thresholds: 90% of the Salary Cap

title: Tax Level set at 121.5% of cap
summary: The Tax Level each year equals 121.5% of the Salary Cap.
detail_paraphrase: For each Salary Cap Year, the Tax Level is fixed at one hundred twenty-one and one-half percent of that year's Salary Cap. (Example: a $134M cap yields a $162.81M Tax Level.)
thresholds: 121.5% of the Salary Cap

title: First Apron Level calculation
summary: The First Apron Level is anchored to the 2023-24 figure and scales with the cap in later years.
detail_paraphrase: For 2023-24, the First Apron Level equals the 2023-24 Tax Level plus $6.716 million multiplied by a fraction whose numerator is the average of the 2022-23 and 2023-24 Salary Caps and whose denominator is the 2022-23 Salary Cap. For each later year, the First Apron Level equals the 2023-24 First Apron Level multiplied by a fraction (current-year Salary Cap over 2023-24 Salary Cap). For these calculations the Salary Cap used is the cap under Sections 2(a)(1)-(3) without the Shortfall/Overage adjustments of 2(a)(5)-(6).
exceptions: The cap used as the scaling input ignores Section 2(a)(5) and 2(a)(6) Shortfall/Overage adjustments
thresholds: 2023-24: Tax Level + $6.716M x (avg of 2022-23 & 2023-24 caps / 2022-23 cap); later years: 2023-24 First Apron x (current cap / 2023-24 cap)

title: Second Apron Level calculation
summary: The Second Apron Level is anchored to the 2023-24 figure (Tax Level + $17.5M) and scales with the cap.
detail_paraphrase: For 2023-24, the Second Apron Level equals the 2023-24 Tax Level plus $17.5 million. For each later year, it equals the 2023-24 Second Apron Level multiplied by a fraction (current-year Salary Cap over 2023-24 Salary Cap). As with the First Apron, the cap input ignores the Shortfall/Overage adjustments in Sections 2(a)(5)-(6).
exceptions: The cap used as the scaling input ignores Section 2(a)(5) and 2(a)(6) Shortfall/Overage adjustments
thresholds: 2023-24: Tax Level + $17.5M; later years: 2023-24 Second Apron x (current cap / 2023-24 cap)

title: Shortfall Amount increases cap and tiers
summary: When there is a Shortfall Amount and no Carryover, the next year's cap, minimum, tax, and apron levels each rise by the per-team Shortfall.
detail_paraphrase: Beginning with 2023-24, if a year has a Shortfall Amount and the Carryover Amount for the next year is zero, then the Salary Cap, Minimum Team Salary, Tax Level, First Apron Level, and Second Apron Level for the next year are each increased by the Shortfall Amount divided by the number of teams that next year (excluding Expansion Teams in their first two Salary Cap Years).
conditions: A Shortfall Amount exists for the year
The next year's Carryover Amount equals zero
exceptions: Expansion Teams in their first two Salary Cap Years are excluded from the divisor
Subject to the floor/cap collar in CAP-010
thresholds: Increase = Shortfall Amount / number of eligible teams

title: Overage Amount reduces cap and tiers
summary: An Overage Amount above 6% of Total Salaries and Benefits reduces next year's cap, minimum, tax, and apron levels via a multi-step formula.
detail_paraphrase: Beginning with 2023-24, if a year's Overage Amount exceeds 6% of Total Salaries and Benefits, the next year's Salary Cap, Minimum Team Salary, Tax Level, First Apron Level, and Second Apron Level are each reduced. Step 1: subtract 6% of Total Salaries and Benefits from the Overage Amount. Step 2: if next-year Projected BRI does not exceed current BRI by more than 8%, OR the Overage exceeds 9% of Total Salaries and Benefits, divide the Step 1 result by the number of eligible teams (that is the reduction). Otherwise (Projected BRI exceeds 108% of BRI and Overage is at or below 9%): Step 3 subtract 108% of current BRI from next-year Projected BRI; Step 4 multiply by 50%; Step 5 subtract that from the Step 1 result (if below zero, no adjustment); Step 6 divide by the number of eligible teams to get the per-tier reduction.
conditions: Overage Amount exceeds 6% of Total Salaries and Benefits
exceptions: No reduction if Step 5 result is below zero
Expansion Teams in first two Salary Cap Years excluded from divisor
Subject to the floor/cap collar in CAP-010
thresholds: Trigger >6% of Total Salaries and Benefits; BRI-growth test at 108% (8%) of prior BRI; 9% Overage cap; 50% BRI-growth offset

title: Year-over-year floor and ceiling on cap and tiers
summary: No cap, minimum, tax, or apron level may fall below the prior year's value or exceed 110% of it.
detail_paraphrase: Despite all other calculation rules, in no event may the Salary Cap, Minimum Team Salary, Tax Level, First Apron Level, or Second Apron Level for a year (a) decrease below its amount for the immediately preceding year, or (b) increase above 110% of its amount for the immediately preceding year.
thresholds: Floor: prior-year value; Ceiling: 110% of prior-year value

title: Tax Bracket Amount scales from $5M base
summary: The Tax Bracket Amount equals $5 million scaled by the ratio of the current cap to the 2023-24 cap.
detail_paraphrase: For a Salary Cap Year, the Tax Bracket Amount equals $5 million multiplied by a fraction whose numerator is that year's Salary Cap and whose denominator is the 2023-24 Salary Cap. For 2023-24 it is $5 million; for a $140.7M 2024-25 cap it would be $5.25 million.
thresholds: $5M x (current cap / 2023-24 cap)

title: Luxury tax owed above the Tax Level (Standard and Repeater rates)
summary: A team whose Tax Team Salary exceeds the Tax Level pays an incremental tax, at higher Repeater rates if it was a taxpayer in 3+ of the prior 4 years.
detail_paraphrase: Any team whose Tax Team Salary exceeds the Tax Level must pay a tax to the NBA, computed on incremental brackets defined in multiples of the Tax Bracket Amount above the Tax Level. Standard Tax Rates apply to teams not over the Tax Level in 3+ of the prior 4 years; Repeater Tax Rates apply to teams over the Tax Level in 3+ of the prior 4 years. From 2025-26 onward the lowest Standard bracket rate is $1.00-for-$1 (vs $1.50-for-$1 in 2023-24/2024-25), and rates step up each successive 100%-of-bracket increment; Repeater rates are higher at every bracket.
conditions: Team's Tax Team Salary exceeds the Tax Level for the year
exceptions: Repeater rates apply only if over the Tax Level in 3+ of prior 4 years
applies_to: all teams over the Tax Level
thresholds: Bracket width = Tax Bracket Amount; Standard 2025-26+ starts $1.00-for-$1 stepping +$0.50 per 100% increment; Repeater starts $3.00-for-$1 (2025-26+); Repeater trigger = over Tax Level in 3 of prior 4 years
notes: Full bracket tables span printed pp.183-184; rates differ between 2023-24/2024-25 and 2025-26-onward columns.

title: Tax Team Salary definition (tax snapshot and adjustments)
summary: Tax Team Salary is a team's Team Salary measured at its last regular-season game, with specified incentive, suspension, and minimum-salary adjustments.
detail_paraphrase: Tax Team Salary is the team's Team Salary as of the start of its last regular-season game (calculated as for Total Salaries and Benefits in the Audit Report), then: plus Incentive Compensation excluded under 3(d) but actually earned; minus Incentive Compensation included under 3(d) but not actually earned; plus any trade-bonus portion earned in a post-season trade that is in Team Salary; plus any amount added under 4(a)(1)(iii); minus 50% of any Compensation reduction from an NBA (not team) suspension; and plus, for a Standard NBA Contract with a Free Agent having 0 or 1 Years of Service, the amount by which the 2-Years-of-Service minimum salary exceeds the contract's salary (with stated treatment for two-way and 10-day-converted free agents).
thresholds: Suspension offset = 50% of NBA-imposed Compensation reduction; 0-or-1-Year free agent uplift to 2-Year minimum salary

title: Interim values used when Audit Report is unavailable
summary: If the Audit Report is not done and no Projected BRI agreement exists, the cap and tiers are set using interim estimates.
detail_paraphrase: If the prior-year Audit Report is not complete by the last day of that year and the NBA and Players Association have not agreed on Projected BRI and Projected Benefits, the next year's Salary Cap, Minimum Team Salary, Tax Level, and apron levels are calculated under the normal rules but using Interim Projected BRI instead of Projected BRI, Estimated BRI instead of BRI, and Estimated Total Salaries and Benefits instead of Total Salaries and Benefits. If even the Interim Audit Report is not complete and no projection agreement exists, the cap is temporarily set as it would have been for the preceding year using the following season's national broadcast rights fees.
conditions: Audit Report (or Interim Audit Report) not completed by last day of the year
No NBA/PA agreement on Projected BRI and Projected Benefits

title: Effective period of cap and tier figures
summary: The cap, minimum, tax, and apron levels apply from the first day through the last day of the Salary Cap Year.
detail_paraphrase: The Salary Cap, Minimum Team Salary, Tax Level, First Apron Level, and Second Apron Level for a Salary Cap Year are in effect from the first day of that year through and including its last day.

title: Basic cap rule: Team Salary may not exceed the cap
summary: A team's Team Salary may never exceed the Salary Cap unless it uses an Exception.
detail_paraphrase: At any time, a team's Team Salary may not exceed the Salary Cap unless the team is using one of the Exceptions provided in Section 6.
exceptions: Section 6 Exceptions permit Team Salary above the cap (separate exceptions bucket)

title: Room and first-year contract limit
summary: A team with Room may sign a contract whose first-year salary does not exceed its current Room.
detail_paraphrase: Subject to the rest of the agreement (including Article II, Section 7), a team that has Room may enter a Player Contract calling for a first-year salary that does not exceed the team's then-current Room.
conditions: Team has Room
thresholds: First-year salary not exceeding current Room

title: Minimum Team Salary shortfall payment and tax-share forfeiture
summary: A team whose MTS Payment Team Salary falls short of the Minimum Team Salary must pay the difference to the NBA and forfeits its tax-distribution share.
detail_paraphrase: If a team's MTS Payment Team Salary for a year is less than the applicable Minimum Team Salary, the NBA requires the team to pay the NBA the difference, and (subject to the 2023-24 carve-out) the team is barred from receiving a share of any tax amount the NBA distributes to non-taxpaying teams that year. MTS Payment Team Salary is the team's MTS Cap Hold Team Salary at the start of the first regular-season day, plus salary excluded under 4(h), minus salary included under 3(e), plus salary excluded under 4(b).
conditions: Team's MTS Payment Team Salary is below the Minimum Team Salary
exceptions: 2023-24 carve-out in CAP-021 may restore a 50% tax-distribution share
applies_to: teams below the Minimum Team Salary
thresholds: Payment = Minimum Team Salary minus MTS Payment Team Salary

title: Minimum Team Salary cap hold during the Regular Season
summary: During the season a team's Team Salary is grossed up by any shortfall of its MTS cap-hold salary below the Minimum Team Salary.
detail_paraphrase: From the first day of the Regular Season through the end of the Salary Cap Year, a team's Team Salary includes the amount (if any) by which the Minimum Team Salary exceeds the lesser of the team's then-current MTS Cap Hold Team Salary and its MTS Cap Hold Team Salary at the start of the first regular-season day. If during the season the team's MTS Cap Hold Team Salary drops below its MTS Threshold, the team must raise it back to at least the MTS Threshold by the end of the following day. The MTS Threshold is the lesser of the Minimum Team Salary and the team's MTS Cap Hold Team Salary at the start of the first regular-season day.
conditions: During the Regular Season through end of the Salary Cap Year
thresholds: Add-on = Minimum Team Salary minus lesser of current/season-start MTS Cap Hold Team Salary; cure deadline = end of following day

title: Year-end Minimum Team Salary shortfall true-up
summary: If actual year-end MTS cap-hold salaries plus any prior payment still fall short of the Minimum Team Salary, the team pays the remaining gap.
detail_paraphrase: If at the end of the year the Minimum Team Salary exceeds the portion of total MTS Cap Hold Team Salaries for which the team is financially responsible plus any payment already required under 2(c)(2)(i), the team pays the NBA the excess. For this computation, MTS Cap Hold Team Salaries include Incentive Compensation that was excluded under 3(d) but actually earned, and exclude Incentive Compensation included under 3(d) but not actually earned. These shortfall payments (under 2(c)(2)(i) and 2(c)(5)) are due within 10 business days after the Governing Audit Report is completed, and the NBA redistributes them equally to all teams within 10 business days of receipt.
conditions: Year-end responsible MTS Cap Hold Team Salaries plus prior payment are below the Minimum Team Salary
applies_to: teams below the Minimum Team Salary at year end
thresholds: Payment = shortfall vs Minimum Team Salary; due within 10 business days of Governing Audit Report; redistributed equally within 10 business days

title: 2023-24 below-minimum non-taxpayer 50% tax-share carve-out
summary: For 2023-24 only, a below-minimum team that owes no tax still receives a 50% share of any distributed tax amounts.
detail_paraphrase: For the 2023-24 year only, if a team's MTS Payment Team Salary is below the Minimum Team Salary but the team owes no Tax, it is entitled to a 50% share of any tax amount the NBA distributes to non-taxpaying teams. Such a team's distribution fraction has a numerator of 0.5 while the other non-taxpaying teams use a numerator of 1, both over a common denominator (e.g., 23.5 when there are 24 non-taxpayers and one is below the minimum).
conditions: 2023-24 Salary Cap Year only
Team's MTS Payment Team Salary below the Minimum Team Salary
Team owes no Tax that year
thresholds: 50% share; distribution fraction numerator 0.5 vs 1 over shared denominator

title: Team Salary may exceed the minimum but not the cap
summary: A team may carry Team Salary above the Minimum Team Salary so long as it does not exceed the cap plus authorized Exceptions.
detail_paraphrase: Nothing prevents a team from having Team Salary above the Minimum Team Salary, provided the Team Salary does not exceed the Salary Cap plus any additional amounts authorized by the Article VII Exceptions.
exceptions: Exceptions under Article VII can authorize Team Salary above the cap (separate exceptions bucket)

title: Tax revenue use and distribution
summary: Tax amounts belong to the NBA; up to 50% may go to non-taxpaying teams and the rest to League purposes.
detail_paraphrase: All tax amounts remitted to the NBA are the NBA's exclusive property. The NBA may distribute up to 50% to one or more teams based wholly or partly on their being non-taxpayers that year, and must use the remainder for League purposes selected by the NBA. League-purpose uses (including team assistance plans) may not be allocated based on a team's Team Salary or taxpayer status, except that an assistance plan crediting a team with at least the league-average Team Salary can qualify.
exceptions: Distributions subject to the below-minimum forfeiture (CAP-018) and the 2023-24 carve-out (CAP-021)
thresholds: Up to 50% distributable to non-taxpayers; due within 10 business days of Governing Audit Report

title: Apron Team Salary definition
summary: Apron Team Salary is Team Salary adjusted by a specified list of additions and subtractions used to test the apron levels.
detail_paraphrase: Apron Team Salary equals a team's Team Salary, then: plus all Performance Bonuses excluded under 3(d); plus the 0-or-1-Year free agent uplift amount from 2(d)(1)(i)(F); plus any amount that could be added under 4(a)(1)(iii); minus any Free Agent Amounts under 4(a)(2); plus, for a Restricted Free Agent, the greater of the salary-plus-Unlikely-Bonuses in any outstanding Qualifying Offer (or Maximum Qualifying Offer) or in any First Refusal Exercise Notice; minus unsigned First Round Pick amounts under 4(a)(4); plus any outstanding Required Tender to a First Round Pick; minus any Salary Cap Exception deemed included under 4(a)(7) and 6(n)(2); plus any amount excluded under 4(l); and minus any incomplete-roster cap hold added under 4(f).
notes: Restriction logic on what teams may DO above the aprons lives in the apron-restrictions bucket; this rule only captures how the apron number is computed.

title: Second Apron Team definition and Draft Pick Penalty
summary: A team over the Second Apron at its last regular-season game is a Second Apron Team, which can trigger a frozen-then-penalized first round draft pick.
detail_paraphrase: A Second Apron Team is one whose Apron Team Salary as of the start of its last regular-season game exceeds the Second Apron Level. Beginning 2024-25, a Second Apron Team is barred from trading its first round pick in the draft following the seventh season after that year, and that pick is frozen. Over the next four years, if the team is a Second Apron Team in 2+ of them, that frozen pick becomes subject to the Draft Pick Penalty (it slides to the final first-round slot, regardless of standings). If the team is a Second Apron Team in fewer than 2 of those four years, the pick becomes tradable (without penalty) the day after the regular season of the third such non-Second-Apron year.
conditions: Team's Apron Team Salary exceeds the Second Apron Level at its last regular-season game
Beginning with 2024-25 for the penalty mechanics
exceptions: Pick is freed without penalty if the team is a Second Apron Team in fewer than 2 of the relevant 4 years
thresholds: Frozen pick = 7th season after the qualifying year; penalty trigger = Second Apron Team in 2+ of next 4 years; Draft Pick Penalty = final pick in the first round

title: Expansion Team first-year cap at 66-2/3%
summary: In its first year of play, an Expansion Team's cap is two-thirds of the normal cap, with the minimum at 90% of that.
detail_paraphrase: Expansion Teams generally have the same cap, minimum, tax, and apron levels as other teams, except that in their first year of play an Expansion Team's Salary Cap equals 66-2/3% of the normally calculated cap (the First Year Expansion Team Salary Cap), and its Minimum Team Salary equals 90% of that reduced cap.
conditions: Expansion Team's first Salary Cap Year of play
depends_on_terms: First Year Expansion Team Salary Cap
thresholds: Cap = 66-2/3% of normal cap; Minimum = 90% of that

title: Expansion Team second-year cap at 80%
summary: In its second year of play, an Expansion Team's cap is 80% of the normal cap, with the minimum at 90% of that.
detail_paraphrase: In the Salary Cap Year immediately following its first year of play, an Expansion Team's Salary Cap equals 80% of the normally calculated cap (the Second Year Expansion Team Salary Cap), and its Minimum Team Salary equals 90% of that reduced cap.
conditions: Expansion Team's second Salary Cap Year of play
depends_on_terms: Second Year Expansion Team Salary Cap
thresholds: Cap = 80% of normal cap; Minimum = 90% of that

title: Deferred Compensation counts when earned
summary: Deferred Compensation counts as Salary in the Salary Cap Year of the season in which it is earned.
detail_paraphrase: All contracts signed, extended, or renegotiated after the agreement's date must specify the seasons in which any Deferred Compensation is earned, and that Deferred Compensation is included in the player's Salary for the Salary Cap Year covering the season in which it is earned.
conditions: Contract entered, extended, or renegotiated after the CBA date

title: Over 38 Rule reallocates late-contract salary
summary: In contracts of 4+ seasons running past age 38, certain late-year salaries are reattributed pro rata to earlier years.
detail_paraphrase: For an Over 38 Contract (signed/extended/renegotiated, covering 4+ seasons including one or more seasons starting after the player turns 38), the aggregate salaries from the later of the fourth contract year or the first year covering a post-38th-birthday season are reattributed pro rata to the earlier years based on those years' salaries. Specified carve-outs and modifications apply: a five-year deal with a Prior Team by a Qualifying Veteran Free Agent age 35-36 reattributes only the fifth year; there is no reallocation for a 4-or-fewer-season deal between a Qualifying Veteran Free Agent and his Prior Team at age 35-36; and, from two years before the First Zero Year, undterminated late salaries are aggregated and split equally across up to three years. Defined terms include Zero Year and First Zero Year.
conditions: Contract covers 4+ seasons
Includes one or more seasons starting after the player reaches age 38
exceptions: No reallocation for a 35-36 Qualifying Veteran Free Agent re-signing with Prior Team for 4 or fewer seasons
Modified single-year reallocation for a 35-36 five-season Prior-Team deal
Players signed under 8(e)(1) are not Qualifying Veteran Free Agents here
thresholds: Trigger: 4+ seasons including a post-age-38 season; aggregation window: up to 3 years before First Zero Year

title: Signing bonuses defined and prorated
summary: Signing bonuses (including trade-triggered and excess international payments) are prorated across contract years by protected base compensation.
detail_paraphrase: For Salary purposes, a signing bonus includes any amount earned on contract signing, any bonus earned upon a trade of the contract, and international payments above the Excluded International Player Payment Amount. A signing bonus is allocated across the contract's Salary Cap Years (or current-and-remaining years for trade bonuses) in proportion to each year's percentage of Base Compensation protected for lack of skill; if an ETO exists, only years before the ETO's Effective Season are used; and if no base compensation is protected for lack of skill, the entire bonus goes to the first year (or, for a trade bonus, the year of the trade).
exceptions: ETO contracts allocate only over pre-ETO years
If none of base compensation is protected for lack of skill, full bonus loads into the first/trade year
thresholds: Allocation weighted by % of Base Compensation protected for lack of skill
notes: Section 3(b)(3) extension-specific signing-bonus mechanics (pp.201-205) are detailed sub-rules not separately extracted here; cited if needed.

title: Incentive Compensation: likely bonuses count, unlikely do not
summary: A Performance Bonus counts in Salary only if it would have been earned based on the prior year's performance (Likely); unlikely bonuses are excluded.
detail_paraphrase: Each year, a Performance Bonus is included in Salary only if it would be earned assuming team/player performance identical to the immediately preceding year (i.e., Likely bonuses count, Unlikely do not). The NBA or Players Association may challenge this through a jointly selected Expert when the prior year does not fairly predict the likelihood; for rookies or veterans who did not play the prior year, the bonus counts if it is likely to be earned. During any such proceeding, the player's salary plus the full disputed bonus is counted in Team Salary. All Incentive Compensation described in Article II Sections 3(b)(iii) and 3(c) is included in Salary.
exceptions: Expert determination can include an Unlikely bonus or exclude a Likely bonus
Rookies/non-playing veterans use a 'likely to be earned' test
thresholds: Likely if earned under identical prior-year performance; disputed bonus fully counted during proceeding

title: International player payments above excluded amount become Salary
summary: International release/inducement payments above the year's Excluded International Player Payment Amount are deemed Salary; amounts at or below it are not.
detail_paraphrase: Payments by an NBA team to a foreign team or other party to induce or secure the right to sign an internationally-playing professional are deemed Salary (as a signing bonus) to the extent they exceed the year's Excluded International Player Payment Amount; amounts up to that excluded amount to secure a contractual release are not Salary. The excluded amount rises annually ($825,000 in 2023-24 up to $975,000 in 2029-30), may be used in whole or part on any new contract but not more than once per three-year period for the same player, is deemed used as of the contract date, does not count toward the Minimum Team Salary, and cannot be used for Two-Way or Exhibit 10 contracts.
conditions: NBA team makes an inducement/release payment for an internationally-playing professional
exceptions: Up to the Excluded International Player Payment Amount for a release is not Salary
Cannot be used for Two-Way Contracts or Exhibit 10 contracts
Does not count toward Minimum Team Salary

title: Salary exclusions: minimum-contract reimbursement, insurance, conduct reductions
summary: Certain amounts are removed from Salary: league-reimbursed minimum-contract portions, life-insurance premium reimbursements, and conduct-related compensation reductions.
detail_paraphrase: The Salary of a player on a one-year, 10-day, or rest-of-season minimum contract is the lesser of the minimum salary or the portion not reimbursed from the league-wide benefits fund. Reimbursed life-insurance premiums under Article II Section 4(j)(ii) are not included in Salary. A player's Salary is computed without regard to conduct-related compensation reductions under Article VI Section 1 or Article XLI Section 4(e) (though this does not apply to Adjustment Salary under Section 12). Loans to players have imputed-interest and protected-compensation limits, and Averaging may deem each year's Salary to be the contract average in certain circumstances.
exceptions: Conduct-reduction exclusion does not apply to Adjustment Salary under Section 12
thresholds: Minimum-contract Salary = lesser of minimum or non-reimbursed portion; loan target rate = Prime + 1% (floor 7%, ceiling 9%)
notes: Bundles several smaller Section 3 exclusion/treatment rules (loans 3(c), one-year minimums 3(f), insurance 3(g), averaging 3(h), conduct reductions 3(i), existing contracts 3(j)). Flagged because the bundling collapses distinct provisions; split into separate rules if finer granularity is needed for compliance checks.

title: Team Salary inclusions
summary: Team Salary aggregates active and certain former players' salaries plus waived/retired/grievance amounts, free agent amounts, offer sheets, draft and incomplete-roster holds, and deemed exceptions.
detail_paraphrase: Team Salary includes the aggregate salaries of all active players (and former players where provided), specifically including: salaries owed on contracts terminated via waiver (or the stretched amount if the team elects stretch); amounts owed to retired players (pro-rated over remaining years by unearned protected compensation); grievance/settlement amounts (with a 50% disputed-amount rule and timing/tax-true-up mechanics); salaries from disclosed conditional agreements; Free Agent Amounts for Veteran Free Agents; salaries under all outstanding Offer Sheets; the unsigned First Round Pick hold; the incomplete-roster charge; includable retired-player consideration under Article XIII Section 5; any Salary Cap Exception deemed included under 6(n)(2); and any Minimum Team Salary add-on under 2(c)(3).
exceptions: Disclosed-agreement salaries are excluded to the extent below the player's Free Agent Amount
Stretch election changes the waived-contract allocation
thresholds: Grievance inclusion = 50% of disputed amount pending resolution
notes: Grievance tax true-up sub-mechanics (4(a)(1)(iii)) are summarized, not fully enumerated.

title: Free Agent Amounts (cap holds for Veteran Free Agents)
summary: A Veteran Free Agent stays on his Prior Team's Team Salary at a percentage-of-prior-salary cap hold until he re-signs, signs elsewhere, or is renounced.
detail_paraphrase: Until a Veteran Free Agent re-signs, signs with another team, or is renounced, his Prior Team carries a Free Agent Amount: a Qualifying Veteran Free Agent at 150% of prior salary (190% if prior salary was below the Estimated Average Player Salary), or 250%/300% following the second Rookie Scale option year; an Early Qualifying Veteran Free Agent at 130%; a Non-Qualifying Veteran Free Agent at 120%. Floors/ceilings apply: minimum-salary players carry the non-reimbursed minimum portion; the amount may not exceed the player's Maximum Player Salary nor drop below the non-reimbursed minimum; rookie-scale second/third-year free agents are capped per 6(n)(3); and a completed Two-Way player carries the zero-Years-of-Service minimum. 'Prior Salary' is prior-season Regular Salary plus signing-bonus allocation and actually-earned incentive compensation.
conditions: Veteran Free Agent not yet re-signed, signed elsewhere, or renounced
exceptions: Minimum-salary prior players use the non-reimbursed minimum hold
Capped at Maximum Player Salary and at 6(n)(3) limits
Completed Two-Way player uses 0-Years-of-Service minimum
thresholds: Qualifying VFA 150%/190% (250%/300% post-2nd-option-year); Early Qualifying 130%; Non-Qualifying 120%; floor = non-reimbursed minimum; ceiling = Maximum Player Salary

title: First Round Pick cap hold (Rookie Scale Cap Hold Amount)
summary: A drafted First Round Pick counts at 120% of his Rookie Scale Amount until he signs or the team loses/assigns/renounces his rights.
detail_paraphrase: Immediately upon being drafted, a First Round Pick is included in the rights-holding team's Team Salary at 120% of his applicable Rookie Scale Amount (the Rookie Scale Cap Hold Amount), and remains so until he signs, or the team loses, assigns, or renounces its exclusive rights. The hold is excluded while the pick is under a non-NBA contract (re-added the following July 1 or when that contract ends), and a team may elect to exclude the hold before any regular season by filing a written non-signing statement plus the player's renunciation of the Required Tender. If an unsigned First Round Pick remains unsigned past the relevant year, the applicable Rookie Scale Amount is recomputed as if he were drafted in the immediately preceding draft at his original draft position.
conditions: Player selected as a First Round Pick
Team holds his exclusive draft rights
exceptions: Excluded while under a non-NBA contract
Excludable by election with player's Required Tender renunciation
thresholds: 120% of applicable Rookie Scale Amount

title: Incomplete roster charge (fewer than 12 players)
summary: From July 1 to the day before the regular season, a roster counted at fewer than 12 is charged the zero-Years-of-Service minimum for each missing slot.
detail_paraphrase: If at any time from July 1 through the day before the regular season a team has fewer than 12 counted players in its Team Salary, its Team Salary is increased by (12 minus the counted players) multiplied by the zero-Years-of-Service Minimum Annual Salary for that year. For counting purposes, only players under contract included in Team Salary, free agents included under 4(a)(2), players given Offer Sheets, and unsigned First Round Picks included under 4(e) count.
conditions: Date is from July 1 through the day before the Regular Season
Fewer than 12 counted players in Team Salary
thresholds: Charge = (12 minus counted players) x zero-Years-of-Service Minimum Annual Salary

title: Renouncing a Veteran Free Agent
summary: Renouncing removes a Veteran Free Agent's Free Agent Amount from Team Salary, limiting how the team may re-sign him, with a narrow rescission right.
detail_paraphrase: A team renounces a Veteran Free Agent by written statement (effective no earlier than the July 1 after the contract's last season), removing his Free Agent Amount from Team Salary and limiting the team to re-signing him only with Room, via the Minimum Player Salary Exception, or to a Two-Way Contract. A team may rescind a renunciation made to create Room for an Offer Sheet within two business days of the Prior Team matching, except where doing so would push Team Salary over the cap (or further over the prior overage). A team cannot renounce a Restricted Free Agent.
conditions: Team holds a Veteran Free Agent
Written renunciation statement provided to the NBA
exceptions: Restricted Free Agents cannot be renounced
Rescission barred if it would push Team Salary over the cap or worsen an existing overage
thresholds: Rescission window = 2 business days after match
notes: Source text labels this subsection (g) but cross-references renunciation as 'Section 6(g)' internally; cited per the (g) heading in Section 4.

title: Long-term (career-ending) injury exclusion from Team Salary
summary: A career-ending injured player whose contract is waived may be excluded from Team Salary after a waiting period, subject to medical findings and a 25-game return rule.
detail_paraphrase: A player with a career-ending injury or illness whose contract is terminated via waiver may have his remaining salary excluded from Team Salary, generally starting one year after his last regular-season/Play-In/playoff game (with alternate timing if he played fewer than 10 games in his last season), but never before one year after his first regular-season game on the roster under that contract. A jointly selected physician or Fitness-to-Play Panel determines career-ending status under stated medical standards. If the player later plays 25 NBA regular-season/Play-In/playoff games in a season for any team, the excluded salary is re-included (with retroactive treatment if the 25th is a Play-In/playoff game) unless the exclusion was based on the elevated-spinal-risk standard. Only the team under contract when the injury became known may apply, only during the contract term; a granted exclusion bars re-signing the player, and stretched salary is also excluded.
conditions: Player suffers a career-ending injury or illness
Contract terminated via the NBA waiver procedure
Applicable waiting period satisfied
exceptions: 25-game return re-inclusion does not apply if exclusion was under the 4(h)(2)(ii) elevated-spinal-risk standard
A team that requested a Disabled Player Exception for that player that year cannot also apply under 4(h)
thresholds: Earliest exclusion = 1 year after last game (alt. 60-day rule if <10 games last season); re-inclusion trigger = 25 NBA games

title: Team Salary exclusions: assigned contracts timing, expansion waivers, two-way, summer, Exhibit 10, second round pick
summary: Specified contract types are excluded from or specially timed in Team Salary: assigned contracts count fully on assignment, while two-way, summer, Exhibit 10 bonus, and second-round-pick-exception contracts are excluded until set dates.
detail_paraphrase: On assignment, the assignee team includes the entire current-and-future-year salary of the assigned contract. Salary of an expansion-draft player waived before the Expansion Team's first season is excluded except (to the extent paid) for the team's minimum obligation. Two-Way Player salaries are excluded from Team Salary (no Room or Exception needed to sign/convert). Summer Contracts are excluded from Team Salary until the first day of the next regular season (with strict limits and a termination-or-Room/Exception requirement). Exhibit 10 Bonus amounts are excluded from Team Salary. A Second Round Pick Exception contract signed July 1-30 is excluded until July 31 of that year.
exceptions: Expansion-waiver salary still counts toward the team's minimum to the extent paid
thresholds: Summer Contract excluded until first day of next Regular Season; Second Round Pick Exception excluded until July 31
notes: Bundles several Section 4 exclusion subsections (b expansion, c assigned, i summer, j two-way, k Exhibit 10, l second round pick). Flagged because the Second Round Pick Exception and Summer Contract are arguably 'exception' constructs that may belong partly in the exceptions bucket; their Team Salary timing/exclusion effect is captured here per scope (what's included/excluded in Team Salary).
